_metadata.description: Restructured questionnaire based on workshop feedback suggestions

info.title: InsectAI hardware database
info.description: A questionnaire to collect information about insect monitoring hardware devices for the InsectAI COST Action hardware database. For more details see: https://github.com/InsectAI-COST-Action/hardware-db

questions.title: Do you want to submit a new device, or update an existing entry?
questions.description: Unsure if you have already submitted? You can check what has already been submitted to the database here: https://insectai-cost-action.github.io/hardware-db/

sections.title: Basic information
sections.description:
Core details about the device and its contact person. 

 Important: all this information will be publicly accessible!

questions.title: Contact person name
questions.description: The person who should be contacted about this database entry. This does not have to be the device designer: it can be a user, project manager, lab lead, or maintainer.

questions.title: Contact email
questions.description:
A valid email address (e.g. name@institution.org) for the contact person above. 

 Please note this email address will be publicly visible!

questions.title: Device name
questions.description:
The common or published name of the device (e.g. 'AMI-trap', 'InsectDetect', 'PitfallCam'). If the device has no established name, use a short descriptive label. 

 Important: this name will be used as a basis to create a unique deviceID in the database; if a record for a deviceID already exists, it will be overwritten (this can be reversed by database maintainers). 
 You can check for existing deviceID using ths page: https://insectai-cost-action.github.io/hardware-db/

questions.title: Device description
questions.description: A short abstract (max 300 characters) explaining what the device is and does, for a non-specialist audience. Focus on purpose and key features rather than technical specifications here.

questions.title: Contributor name (can be the same as contact name)
questions.description: The person filling in this form. May differ from the device creator if someone else is submitting on their behalf.

questions.title: Contributor email (can be the same as contact email)
Institution name(s)
questions.description: The institution(s) affiliated with this device or project. Separate multiple institutions with ';' (e.g. 'University of Edinburgh; NERC').

questions.title: Device creator(s)
questions.description: The person(s) who originally designed or built this device. Separate multiple names with ';' (e.g. 'Alan Turner; Dave Johnson'). This may differ from the contributor submitting this form.

questions.title: Device creator email(s)
questions.description: Email address(es) for the creator(s) above, in the same order, separated by ';'.

questions.title: Maintainer name
questions.description: The person currently responsible for maintaining or updating the device design. Leave blank if the same as the creator.

questions.title: Device version name
questions.description: A label for this specific version of the device (e.g. 'v2.1', '2024-field-edition'). Useful when multiple versions exist.

questions.title: Device licence (e.g. CC-BY-4.0)
questions.description: The licence under which the device design and associated materials are released. Use a standard SPDX identifier where possible (e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0', 'MIT', 'CERN-OHL-S-2.0'). Leave blank if unknown.

questions.title: Device construction
questions.description: Select all that apply. 'Off-the-shelf' means the device is used as purchased with no modification. 'Partly custom' includes devices assembled from standard components with some user-designed parts (e.g. a 3D-printed enclosure or custom PCB). 'Fully custom' means the device was designed and fabricated entirely by the user.
options: Modified off-the-shelf: Pre-built device with user-made adjustments or upgrades
Partly custom: Assembled from off-the-shelf and/or open-source components with some user design or modification
Fully custom: Designed and fabricated by the user (hardware and potentially software)

questions.title: Device cost (€) - excluding operational costs
questions.description: Approximate unit build cost for the hardware only (components, PCBs, enclosure, etc.). Do not include deployment consumables, cloud subscriptions, or labour costs.

questions.title: Power source(s)
questions.description: Select all power sources that can be used to operate the device.

questions.title: Power duration under continuous use
questions.description: How long the device can run on a single charge or battery set during continuous operation (e.g. '8 hours', '3 days'). Enter 'N/A' if mains-powered only.

questions.title: Power duration under standard use
questions.description: How long the device operates between charges or battery changes under typical deployment conditions (e.g. motion-triggered, scheduled intervals). Enter 'N/A' if mains-powered only.

questions.title: Processing unit
questions.description: The main compute component of the device (e.g. 'Raspberry Pi 4', 'NVIDIA Jetson Nano', 'Arduino Uno', 'ESP32'). Include model name and version where known.

questions.title: Model processing
questions.description: Where detection or classification models are run. 'On-device' means inference happens on the device itself. 'Offboard' means data is transferred to another computer or the cloud before processing.
options: Local computing (near edge processing using locally connected computers on the network)
Offboard processing (data transfer to and processing on separate computer)

questions.title: Repairability score
questions.description: Rate from 1 (hardest) to 5 (easiest). 1 = requires soldering or specialist tools; 2 = requires tools but no specialist skills; 3 = screwdriver assembly, standard parts; 4 = snap-fit or modular replacement; 5 = fully tool-free, hot-swap components.

questions.title: Firmware update frequency
questions.description: How often firmware updates are typically released or applied (e.g. 'monthly', 'as needed', 'once per season', 'never').

questions.title: Firmware update method
questions.description: How firmware is delivered to the device (e.g. 'Over-the-Air (OTA)', 'USB cable', 'SD card', 'SSH').

sections.title: Intended usage scope and operational constraints

questions.title: Taxonomic group(s)
questions.description: The insect or arthropod groups this device is designed or validated for (e.g. 'Lepidoptera', 'Coleoptera', 'Hymenoptera'). Use scientific names where possible; separate multiple groups with ';'.

questions.title: Operational temperature range (°C)
questions.description: The minimum and maximum ambient temperatures within which the device functions reliably (e.g. '-5 to 40'). Refer to manufacturer specifications or field experience.

questions.title: Weatherproofing
questions.description: The IP (Ingress Protection) rating or equivalent, if known (e.g. 'IP65', 'IP54'). If no formal rating exists, describe the protection level (e.g. 'splash-proof enclosure', 'not weatherproof').

questions.title: Operational costs (€)
questions.description: Estimated running costs for a typical deployment season (e.g. one summer field season). Include consumables (batteries, lures), cloud storage, SIM data plans, etc. Exclude the initial hardware build cost.
